nodes.excerpt: ### REQ-CA-002 — Repository artifact coverage  The graph shall represent repository documents, identified requirement sections, tracked issue drafts, Python source files, and Python test files. Nodes shall have stable identifiers and reposi
nodes.label: Repository artifact coverage

nodes.excerpt: ### REQ-CA-003 — Meaningful, inspectable relationships  The graph shall represent declared requirement, issue, dependency, implementation, and test relationships, plus Python import relationships where available. Every edge shall include pr
nodes.label: Meaningful, inspectable relationships

nodes.excerpt: ### REQ-CA-004 — Distinct progress states  Issue nodes shall expose GitHub state (`draft`, `open`, or `closed`) separately from implementation state (`planned`, `in_progress`, or `complete`). The interface shall use a legend and visually di
nodes.label: Distinct progress states

nodes.excerpt: ### REQ-CA-005 — Interactive traceability  The application shall let a viewer filter node types and states, select a node, inspect its metadata and adjacent relationships, and navigate to provenance evidence sufficient to trace an implement
nodes.label: Interactive traceability

nodes.excerpt: ### REQ-CA-006 — Deterministic context-budget explorer  For a selected issue/task and configurable budget, the application shall show a deterministic ranked set of loadable artifact slices. Each recommendation shall state its estimated cost
nodes.label: Deterministic context-budget explorer

nodes.label: Visible budget effects

nodes.excerpt: ### REQ-CA-008 — Input validation  The builder shall reject malformed metadata, duplicate identifiers, invalid state values, missing referenced paths, and missing referenced node identifiers with actionable diagnostics.
nodes.label: Input validation
